investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-06T00:47–00:54Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler rejection: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the two nodes that carry that resource class, and the remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled, preventing any agent from reaching a running/idle/ready state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner or source-code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-06T00:49–00:54Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm; 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption cannot resolve the shortage. Because the eval pod never scheduled, the runner could not create a remote agent, and therefore no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to fail with all four required fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two nodes that carry that label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, and preemption found no victims to evict. As a result, every eval attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod was rejected as Unschedulable after ~124–146 seconds, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the runner to collect the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 708 minutes old at eval time, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot artifact, not to any web-serving or routing layer.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 708 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-08-06T00:54:36Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred roughly 11 hours and 48 minutes before the eval, well beyond the maxAgeMinutes: 300 contract boundary. This is an eval-layer signal of a stale CI/CD artifact; no evidence of a user-facing web outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 708 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 708 minutes old at eval time, more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot artifact, not to any web-serving or routing layer.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 708 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-08-06T00:54:36Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred roughly 11 hours and 48 minutes before the eval, well beyond the maxAgeMinutes: 300 contract boundary. This is an eval-layer signal of a stale CI/CD artifact; no evidence of a user-facing web outage is present in the supplied packet.

expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact boundary breached.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 and valid app shells — the public website itself is reachable and serving correctly, ruling out a broad infrastructure failure.
source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational' — this failure does not constitute a declared service outage in the feature registry.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2170: runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) — the eval directly reads the live published artifact, confirming the staleness is in the artifact itself, not in the eval runner logic.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was skipped, cancelled, or failed silently in the ~12 hours preceding the eval run, leaving the previously published artifact in place without an update.
Second: A GitHub Actions runner quota, billing limit, or scheduled trigger misconfiguration caused the snapshot-publishing workflow to not be queued or to time out before completing the publish step.
Third: The publish step in the workflow completed but wrote to a different path or branch, so the file at the canonical snapshotUrl was not updated even though a workflow run nominally succeeded.

Fourth: A GitHub Pages propagation delay or CDN caching issue caused the eval to read a stale cached version of status.json even though a fresh file was published — less likely given the 708-minute gap far exceeds typical CDN TTLs.

Fifth: The eval runner's clock or the snapshot's embedded timestamp is incorrect, causing snapshotAgeMinutes to be computed incorrectly — less likely because generatedAtPresent=true and all other evidence fields are structurally consistent.
